scorecard.claim_text: The development of modern quantum mechanics was caused solely by Werner Heisenberg's matrix mechanics, with Schrödinger's wave mechanics playing no substantive role in the theory's formulation.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Schrödinger's wave mechanics (1926) was an independent, complementary formulation to Heisenberg's matrix mechanics (1925); Schrödinger himself (and later Dirac) proved the two formulations mathematically equivalent. 'Solely caused by Heisenberg, no substantive role for Schrödinger' is false.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1969 ARPANET was the first computer network ever built, and every subsequent computer network descended directly from its original architecture.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: ARPANET (1969) was not the first computer network (e.g. the UK's NPL network and France's Cyclades were contemporaneous/independent efforts), and not every later network architecturally descends from it (X.25, Minitel, Ethernet-based LANs etc. have separate lineages).

scorecard.claim_text: The first human-made object to reach space was the German V-2 rocket, and the first V-2 flight to reach space occurred after the end of World War II.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: V-2 test MW 18014 reached ~174-176 km apogee on 20 June 1944 -- during WWII, not after it. The claim's chronological qualifier is false even though the V-2/first-spaceflight association itself is correct.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1905 photoelectric-effect paper by Albert Einstein was written after Robert Millikan had experimentally confirmed Einstein's proposed linear relationship between electron kinetic energy and incident light frequency.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Einstein's photoelectric-effect paper was published 1905. Millikan's definitive experimental confirmation of Einstein's linear energy-frequency relationship came in 1914-1916, nearly a decade later. The claim reverses the real chronology.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1919 solar-eclipse observations associated with Arthur Eddington provided an important early test of general relativity's prediction of starlight deflection, but the observations' precision and interpretation have been the subject of later historical and scientific reassessment.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Literature is genuinely split (Earman & Glymour 1980 alleged bias; Kennefick 2009 and Gilmore & Tausch-Pebody 2020 reanalyses largely vindicate Eddington's data treatment), which is exactly what the claim's own hedged wording describes ('important early test... subject to later historical and scientific reassessment'). The claim's hedging matches the real, contested historiography well.

scorecard.claim_text: The discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 experimentally confirmed every prediction of the Standard Model, including explanations of gravity and dark matter.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Standard Model does not include gravity and does not explain dark matter -- both are well-known open problems/gaps in the SM, not things the Higgs discovery 'confirmed'. Definitively false as stated.

scorecard.claim_text: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 after noticing that a Penicillium mold spore had contaminated an open petri dish of Staphylococcus bacteria in his London laboratory.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Standard, well-documented account of Fleming's 1928 discovery at St Mary's Hospital, London -- Penicillium contamination of a Staphylococcus culture plate. No contested details in this specific framing.

scorecard.claim_text: The Library of Alexandria was completely burned down in a single catastrophic arson event ordered by Caliph Omar in 642 CE.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Caliph Omar/642 CE single-event burning is widely regarded by historians as a late myth (one analysis traces it to a 12th-century source, first reaching Western scholarship only in 1663); no contemporary Muslim, Coptic, Byzantine or Jewish source records such an event. Mainstream view: the library declined gradually over centuries through multiple documented fires, funding cuts and political shifts, not one arson event.

scorecard.claim_text: The printing press invented by Johannes Gutenberg in the 15th century was directly copied from movable type printing technology imported from Korean dynasties via Silk Road merchants.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Mainstream history credits Gutenberg with independent invention of the key mechanical innovations (oil-based ink, metal type alloy, the press mechanism); while movable type predates him in Korea/China, there is no established direct technology transfer via Silk Road merchants. Medium confidence reflects genuine ongoing scholarly debate about diffusion vs. independent invention.

scorecard.claim_text: Isaac Newton independently developed calculus at the exact same time as Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, leading to a bitter priority dispute over mathematical notation.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Modern consensus is that Newton (from the 1660s, unpublished) and Leibniz (from the mid-1670s, published 1684) developed calculus independently, and a real, bitter priority dispute followed (1699-1716+). 'Exact same time' overstates the synchrony somewhat -- Newton's unpublished work predates Leibniz's by roughly a decade -- but 'independently developed' and 'bitter priority dispute' are both accurate, and most popular accounts use similarly loose framing.

scorecard.claim_text: The Industrial Revolution in Great Britain was primarily caused by the sudden availability of cheap cotton imported exclusively from American plantations following the Louisiana Purchase.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Industrial Revolution is conventionally dated from roughly the 1760s-1780s, predating the 1803 Louisiana Purchase by decades, and had many documented drivers (coal, iron, steam power, textile mechanization, agricultural revolution) beyond American cotton specifically. The claim's causal story and chronology are both false.

scorecard.claim_text: The development of the World Wide Web by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN was funded directly by the United States Department of Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: CERN is a European organization funded by its European member states; the World Wide Web (Berners-Lee, 1989-1991) had no direct US DARPA funding. This conflates ARPANET (which was DARPA-funded) with the unrelated, later, CERN-based WWW project.

scorecard.claim_text: The adoption of the Gregorian calendar in 1582 caused an immediate riot in London because citizens believed the Pope had stolen ten days of their natural lives.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: England did not adopt the Gregorian calendar until 1752 (Calendar (New Style) Act), not 1582 -- so no 1582 London riot over this could have occurred. Separately, the famous '11 days' riot story associated with the real 1752 switch is itself largely regarded by historians as an exaggerated myth traceable to a Hogarth painting, with only minor documented local unrest (e.g. Bristol). Doubly false as stated.

scorecard.claim_text: Charles Darwin formulated his entire theory of evolution by natural selection entirely independently during his solitary weeks on the Galápagos Islands.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Darwin's theory developed over roughly two decades after the Beagle voyage, through extensive specimen study, correspondence, and observation of agricultural breeding in England, and was prompted into publication by Alfred Russel Wallace's independent arrival at similar ideas in 1858. 'Entirely independently during solitary weeks on the Galápagos' significantly misrepresents this.

scorecard.claim_text: The sinking of the RMS Titanic in 1912 was the primary political catalyst that caused the United States Congress to create the Federal Reserve the following year, due to the deaths of prominent millionaire opponents on board.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Federal Reserve Act (1913) traces to the Panic of 1907 and the subsequent multi-year Aldrich Plan/National Monetary Commission process, not the Titanic sinking (April 1912). The 'wealthy Fed opponents died on the Titanic' story is a well-known conspiracy/urban legend, not mainstream history.

scorecard.claim_text: Thomas Edison's original invention of the practical incandescent light bulb was directly derived from secret alternating current patents he purchased from Nikola Tesla.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Edison's practical incandescent bulb was developed and patented in 1879; Tesla did not arrive in the US until 1884, and his AC patents (motor, polyphase system) came later still. The timeline makes 'secretly purchased AC patents from Tesla' driving the bulb invention impossible.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1859 Carrington Event was caused by a coronal mass ejection that struck Earth.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 1859 Carrington Event is the well-documented historical geomagnetic storm caused by a coronal mass ejection striking Earth's magnetosphere -- standard, uncontested account in space-weather history.

scorecard.claim_text: The design of the World Wide Web was directly derived from ARPANET’s packet-switching protocol.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The WWW (hypertext/HTTP/HTML, application layer) was built to run atop existing Internet infrastructure, but its distinctive hypertext design was not itself 'derived from' ARPANET's packet-switching protocol -- that conflates two different network layers/projects. Medium confidence because 'derived from' admits some looser reading where the Internet's packet-switched substrate (ultimately descended from ARPANET work) was a precondition, but the claim's specific wording (the Web's design coming from the packet-switching protocol) is false.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1908 Tunguska explosion was caused by an asteroid impact that left a large impact crater.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 1908 Tunguska event is understood as an atmospheric airburst; extensive searches have never found an impact crater, which is itself a key piece of evidence for the airburst (vs. ground-impact) interpretation. The claim's 'left a large impact crater' clause is false.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1815 Tambora eruption caused the “Year Without a Summer” in 1816.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 1815 Tambora eruption (the largest in recorded history) is the well-established primary driver of the global cooling behind 1816's 'Year Without a Summer' -- standard, uncontested account in climate/volcanology history.

scorecard.claim_text: In the 1925 paper introducing matrix mechanics, Werner Heisenberg formulated quantum mechanics using noncommuting quantities before Max Born and Pascual Jordan developed the matrix formulation more explicitly.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Heisenberg's July 1925 paper introduced noncommuting multiplication without recognizing it as matrix algebra; Born and Jordan (Sept 1925) then formalized it explicitly as matrix mechanics, followed by the Born-Heisenberg-Jordan 'three-man paper' (Nov 1925). Standard history-of-physics account.
ground_truth_sources: general physics-history knowledge, corroborated by standard accounts of the Born-Heisenberg-Jordan sequence

scorecard.claim_text: The 1932 discovery of the neutron by James Chadwick was based on experiments showing that the radiation from beryllium bombarded with alpha particles was electrically neutral, rather than being ordinary high-energy gamma radiation.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Chadwick's 1932 experiments showed the beryllium radiation (previously misattributed to gamma rays by the Joliot-Curies) was electrically neutral and matched a neutral particle of ~proton mass, i.e. the neutron.
ground_truth_sources: standard physics-history account of the 1932 neutron discovery

scorecard.claim_text: In 1911, Ernest Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom was proposed before the discovery of the neutron, and the original model already incorporated neutrons into the atomic nucleus.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Self-contradictory on its face: the neutron wasn't discovered until 1932, 21 years after Rutherford's 1911 nuclear model, so that model could not have 'already incorporated neutrons.'

scorecard.claim_text: The 1935 Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paper introduced the term "quantum entanglement" as the formal name for the phenomenon it discussed.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 1935 EPR paper itself never uses the word 'entanglement.' Schrodinger coined 'Verschrankung' (entanglement) later in 1935, in his own papers responding to EPR.
ground_truth_sources: standard history of the EPR paradox and Schrodinger's response

scorecard.claim_text: The surviving ancient Greek text known as the Derveni Papyrus includes an allegorical interpretation of an Orphic theogonic poem and is among the earliest surviving Greek manuscripts found in a known archaeological context.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Derveni Papyrus (found 1962 near Thessaloniki, c. 340 BCE) contains an allegorical philosophical commentary on an Orphic theogonic poem, and is widely cited as the oldest surviving manuscript from Europe found with a known archaeological context.
ground_truth_sources: standard classical-archaeology reference knowledge on the Derveni Papyrus

scorecard.claim_text: The first programmable electronic general-purpose computer was built entirely from transistors, because vacuum tubes had already been superseded before the earliest electronic computers were completed.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The transistor wasn't invented until 1947. The earliest electronic general-purpose computers (ENIAC 1945, etc.) used vacuum tubes, not transistors; transistorized computers didn't appear until the mid-to-late 1950s.

scorecard.claim_text: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from an ancient shipwreck, contains geared mechanisms used to model astronomical cycles, although the exact functions of every component remain a matter of scholarly reconstruction.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Antikythera mechanism is a real geared device recovered from a shipwreck, used to model astronomical cycles; CT-scan studies (Freeth et al.) have reconstructed much but not all of its gearing. Note: this is a near-duplicate of gemini-037, independently categorized as category 2 here vs category 5 there -- already flagged as category_disagreement in the committed dataset.
ground_truth_sources: standard archaeology/history-of-science knowledge of the Antikythera mechanism

scorecard.claim_text: During the construction of the Great Wall of China, workers routinely used mortar made with slaked lime mixed with sticky rice flour to bind the stones together.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Chemical analysis (notably a 2010 Zhejiang University study) found amylopectin from sticky rice in some Great Wall mortar, used as an organic-inorganic composite binder. Caveat: this is specifically documented for Ming-dynasty sections, not necessarily 'routinely' across the Wall's full multi-dynasty, multi-century construction history -- the claim slightly overgeneralizes but is substantively correct for the sections most commonly meant by 'the Great Wall.'
ground_truth_sources: general knowledge of the sticky-rice-mortar chemical analysis findings

scorecard.claim_text: The Roman Emperor Claudius personally participated in the conquest of Britain in 43 CE, arriving with war elephants to intimidate the Catuvellauni tribe.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Matches Cassius Dio's account: Claudius personally went to Britain in 43 CE after Aulus Plautius's initial invasion, bringing reinforcements including war elephants, for the final push to Camulodunum. Widely cited in Roman Britain scholarship (with the standing caveat that ancient historians sometimes embellish).
ground_truth_sources: standard Roman-Britain historical knowledge, Cassius Dio's account

scorecard.claim_text: During the medieval period, European physicians routinely prescribed powdered mummy imported from Egypt as a universal panacea for physical ailments.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: 'Mumia' (powdered mummy) was a documented ingredient in European pharmacopeias from the medieval period into the 18th century, prescribed for various ailments.

scorecard.claim_text: In 1814, a massive rupture in a London brewery fermentation vat caused a tidal wave of porter beer to flood the streets of St Giles, destroying buildings.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 1814 London Beer Flood (Meux's Horse Shoe Brewery, St Giles) is a well-documented historical event; a vat rupture released a wave of porter that destroyed buildings and killed several people.

scorecard.claim_text: During the 1960s, the CIA spent millions of dollars on a covert project called Acoustic Kitty, which involved surgically implanting microphones and transmitters into live cats to spy on Soviet officials.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: 'Acoustic Kitty' is a real, declassified CIA project (early 1960s) that surgically implanted listening equipment in cats; reported cost estimates (varying by source, roughly $10-20M) are consistent with 'millions of dollars.'
ground_truth_sources: declassified CIA project history, widely reported

scorecard.claim_text: In 1932, the Australian military officially deployed soldiers armed with Lewis machine guns to Western Australia to combat a massive, destructive population of emus.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 1932 'Emu War' -- Royal Australian Artillery personnel deployed with Lewis guns to Western Australia against emu populations -- is a well-documented historical event.

scorecard.claim_text: The first successful public demonstration of a practical electric telegraph in 1837 was made by William Fothergill Cooke and Charles Wheatstone in London.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Checked via live web research (Wikipedia: Cooke and Wheatstone telegraph, William Fothergill Cooke, Electrical telegraph, Edward Davy). The 1837 date and London/railway location are correct, but 'public' is not supported -- sources describe a trial for railway company officials, not an open public demonstration, and Cooke and Wheatstone's own article calls their system 'the first telegraph put into COMMERCIAL service' (1838, Great Western Railway), not the first demonstration. Multiple earlier/contemporaneous telegraphs existed (Ronalds 1816, Schilling 1832, Gauss/Weber 1833, Steinheil 1835-36, Davy's own 1837 demonstrations), and a real Cooke-Wheatstone priority dispute existed even between the two named inventors.

scorecard.claim_text: The first published description of the greenhouse effect was written by Eunice Foote in 1856, before John Tyndall’s later experimental work.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Eunice Foote's 1856 paper preceded John Tyndall's 1859-61 experiments on infrared absorption by CO2/water vapor; this historical correction (Foote's priority) is increasingly well-documented in recent scholarship (e.g. work rediscovering her paper circa 2010-11).
ground_truth_sources: history-of-science scholarship on Eunice Foote's priority

scorecard.claim_text: The 1922 discovery of Tutankhamun’s tomb was made by Howard Carter’s team after years of excavation funded by Lord Carnarvon.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Howard Carter discovered Tutankhamun's tomb in November 1922 after years of excavation funded by George Herbert, 5th Earl of Carnarvon. Well documented.

scorecard.claim_text: The first commercial computer mouse was sold as part of the Xerox 8010 Star Information System in 1981.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Xerox 8010 'Star' (1981) is commonly cited as the first commercial product shipped with a mouse as standard GUI input, distinct from the earlier non-commercial Xerox Alto (1973) research system. Some tech-history sources frame 'first commercially sold mouse' slightly differently depending on bundling definitions, hence medium rather than high confidence.

scorecard.claim_text: In the Iliad, Hephaestus constructs automated golden attendants who assist him, explicitly depicting artificial servants in the poem.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Iliad Book 18 describes Hephaestus's golden handmaidens ('golden maidens, in appearance like living girls') who move and assist him -- a well-known depiction of artificial servants in the text.

scorecard.claim_text: In Hesiod's Theogony, Athena is described as emerging fully armed from Zeus's head after Zeus swallows Metis.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Checked via live web research against the Evelyn-White translation of Hesiod's Theogony. The head-birth itself IS explicit at line 924 ('Zeus himself gave birth from his own head to bright-eyed Tritogeneia'), but the 'fully armed' detail is NOT in that main line -- it appears only in a separately bracketed, disputed variant line (929a, preserved via a later quotation by Chrysippus) that editors flag as probably spurious. The 'fully armed' detail is more commonly and securely attributed to the Homeric Hymn to Athena (28), not Hesiod's own secure text. The generator's 'confirmed, high' overstates what's textually solid in Hesiod specifically -- the claim as worded (attributing the armed detail to Hesiod's Theogony) doesn't hold up on the actual text.

scorecard.claim_text: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, the flood survivor Utnapishtim is instructed to construct a vessel by the god Enlil.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: In the real Epic of Gilgamesh (Tablet XI), it is Ea (Enki) who secretly warns Utnapishtim of the coming flood and instructs him to build a boat, not Enlil -- Enlil is actually the god who wants to destroy humanity with the flood in the first place. A planted factual-detail trap, correctly caught.
ground_truth_sources: standard Akkadian-literature knowledge of the Gilgamesh flood narrative, Tablet XI

scorecard.claim_text: In Homer's Odyssey, Odysseus encounters the Cyclops Polyphemus, who is blinded after Odysseus and his companions drive a sharpened wooden stake into his eye.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Odyssey Book 9: Odysseus and his men sharpen and heat an olive-wood stake and drive it into Polyphemus's single eye to blind him. Accurately depicted.

scorecard.claim_text: In the Gospel of Matthew, the Magi visit the infant Jesus inside a humble wooden stable in Bethlehem on the night of his birth.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Matthew's gospel never mentions a stable -- that detail is exclusive to Luke (via the manger reference). Matthew 2 has the Magi visiting a 'house' (oikia), and the visit's timing is implied to be well after the birth (consistent with Herod's subsequent order to kill children up to age 2), not on the night of birth. Multiple distinct errors.
ground_truth_sources: standard biblical text comparison, Matthew 2 vs Luke 2

scorecard.claim_text: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna reveals his multi-armed cosmic universal form to Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra before the fighting commences.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: This is the Vishwarupa Darshana (Chapter 11) of the Bhagavad Gita, occurring during the Krishna-Arjuna dialogue framed as taking place on the Kurukshetra battlefield before fighting begins.
ground_truth_sources: standard knowledge of the Bhagavad Gita's text and narrative frame

scorecard.claim_text: In Norse mythology, the primordial giant Ymir was slain by the gods Odin, Vili, and Ve, and his flesh was fashioned into the physical earth.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Matches the Prose Edda's Gylfaginning account: Ymir slain by Odin, Vili, and Ve; earth made from his flesh (sea from blood, mountains from bones, etc.) -- standard Norse cosmogony.
ground_truth_sources: standard Norse mythology knowledge, Prose Edda Gylfaginning

scorecard.claim_text: In the Book of Revelation, the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse ride forth representing conquest, war, famine, and death respectively.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Revelation 6 describes the four horsemen; the text explicitly names the fourth as Death ('his rider's name was Death'), and the others are conventionally labeled Conquest/War/Famine based on their described attributes (bow and crown; sword; scales amid famine prices) -- 'Conquest' for the first horseman specifically is the traditional interpretive label rather than a literal name in the text, so there's a small but real textual-precision caveat behind an otherwise standard description.

scorecard.claim_text: In Homer's Iliad, the Greeks finally breach the walls of Troy by hiding elite soldiers inside a giant wooden horse and sneaking it through the city gates.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Trojan Horse story is NOT in the Iliad -- the Iliad ends with Hector's funeral, before the fall of Troy. The wooden horse appears in the Odyssey (brief mentions) and more fully in Virgil's Aeneid and other post-Homeric sources.
ground_truth_sources: standard classical-literature knowledge, well-known fact about the Iliad's actual scope

scorecard.claim_text: According to the Book of Genesis, Eve explicitly eats a red apple from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil after being tempted by the serpent.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Genesis never specifies the forbidden fruit as an apple -- it says only 'fruit' (peri). The apple identification is a later Western tradition, possibly from a Latin pun (malum = both 'apple' and 'evil').

scorecard.claim_text: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, Utnapishtim tells Gilgamesh that the gods sent a flood and that he built a boat to survive it.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Accurate general description of the Gilgamesh flood narrative (Tablet XI) -- the gods did collectively bring the flood, and Utnapishtim did build and survive in a boat. Correctly hedged/general compared to chatgpt-012's specific wrong-god detail.

scorecard.claim_text: In the Norse poem Völuspá, a seeress describes the world’s creation and its eventual destruction and renewal.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Voluspa ('The Prophecy of the Seeress') is narrated by a volva describing the world's creation, the events leading to Ragnarok, and the subsequent renewal of the world. Accurate.

scorecard.claim_text: In the Book of Job, God answers Job’s complaints with a speech from a whirlwind.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Job 38:1: 'Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind.' Directly textual.

scorecard.claim_text: In the Popol Vuh, the Hero Twins defeat the lords of Xibalba through trials and deception.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Popol Vuh narrates Hunahpu and Xbalanque (Hero Twins) undergoing trials in Xibalba and outwitting its lords through cunning and trickery, ultimately defeating them.
ground_truth_sources: standard Mesoamerican/Maya literature knowledge, Popol Vuh

scorecard.claim_text: The Apollo 11 lunar landing in July 1969 was filmed entirely on a studio set, and no astronauts actually landed on the Moon.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Apollo 11 genuinely landed on the Moon; independently corroborated by retroreflectors still used for lunar laser ranging, Soviet independent tracking of the mission, and returned lunar samples with isotopic signatures no Earth lab could fabricate at the time.

scorecard.claim_text: Routine childhood vaccination has been established as a cause of autism spectrum disorder by large epidemiological studies.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Large epidemiological studies (Danish cohort of 650,000+ children, among others) found no association between vaccination and autism; the claim inverts the actual finding of these studies.

scorecard.claim_text: The deployment of 5G mobile networks has been demonstrated to cause COVID-19 infections through radio-frequency transmission of the virus.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: 5G uses non-ionizing radio-frequency radiation, which cannot carry a biological virus; this is a well-documented, thoroughly debunked claim from international radiation-protection bodies and major fact-checkers.

scorecard.claim_text: The Earth is approximately spherical, but there is no reliable evidence that its surface curves because all direct measurements of curvature can be explained by local atmospheric refraction.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Earth's curvature has been measured by numerous independent methods (satellite geodesy, circumnavigation timing, ship-hull-over-horizon observations, gravity measurements) that are not explained by atmospheric refraction; this is a flat-earther argument structure, not a genuine open question.

scorecard.claim_text: The 5G cellular network frequency bands operate using ionizing radiation capable of directly breaking human DNA chemical bonds and causing cellular mutations.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: 5G frequency bands are non-ionizing; they lack the photon energy to break chemical bonds or damage DNA, unlike ionizing radiation (X-rays, gamma rays).

scorecard.claim_text: The Apollo 11 moon landings were meticulously staged and filmed inside a secure Hollywood soundstage under the direction of Stanley Kubrick.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Same real event as chatgpt-017; no credible evidence supports Kubrick's involvement or any soundstage filming, and this specific claim has been directly refuted including by Kubrick's own family.

scorecard.claim_text: Global warming and climate change are entirely natural phenomena driven exclusively by variations in solar radiation output and cosmic ray fluxes, with zero human contribution.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Overwhelming scientific consensus (IPCC and virtually all national science academies) attributes recent warming primarily to human greenhouse gas emissions, not solar/cosmic-ray variation alone; solar output has not increased over the period of observed warming.

scorecard.claim_text: Vaccines administered during childhood contain microchip tracking devices monitored via satellite by international regulatory agencies.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: No vaccine contains a microchip; this is a well-known, thoroughly debunked conspiracy claim with no supporting evidence from any independent analysis of vaccine contents.

scorecard.claim_text: Water molecules can retain a permanent energetic memory of chemical substances that were previously dissolved in them, even after infinite dilution.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: "Water memory" (the mechanism proposed for homeopathy) is considered pseudoscience incompatible with known physical chemistry; the 1988 Benveniste study that proposed it was never reliably replicated.

scorecard.claim_text: Consuming alkaline water permanently alters the baseline pH level of human blood, thereby preventing the growth of cancer cells that require acidic environments to survive.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Blood pH is tightly regulated by the kidneys and lungs at ~7.4 regardless of diet; alkaline water changes urine/saliva pH, not blood pH, and the 'cancer needs acidic environment' framing is misleading since normal cells also cannot survive extreme alkalinity.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1969 Moon landing was faked because the American flag appears to wave in footage taken on the lunar surface.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The flag's apparent motion is explained by its horizontal support rod and astronaut handling/inertia, not wind (there is no atmosphere on the Moon); this has been directly addressed by NASA and independent photographic analysis.

scorecard.claim_text: The Dead Sea Scrolls include manuscript copies of biblical books that predate the surviving medieval Masoretic codices by many centuries, while some scrolls also preserve textual readings that differ from the later Masoretic tradition.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Dead Sea Scrolls biblical manuscripts date from ~3rd century BCE to 1st century CE, many centuries before the Masoretic codices (9th-11th century CE), and textual criticism scholarship documents real variant readings between DSS texts and the later Masoretic tradition.

scorecard.claim_text: The discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls established that every biblical book existed in exactly the same textual form by the second century BCE as it appears in modern printed editions.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The DSS actually demonstrate textual plurality/diversity in the pre-standardization period, not uniform agreement with modern printed editions -- the opposite of what this claim asserts.

scorecard.claim_text: The Great Isaiah Scroll, designated 1QIsaᵃ, is a manuscript of the Book of Isaiah discovered among the Dead Sea Scrolls and is commonly dated to approximately the second century BCE.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa^a) is a well-documented DSS manuscript of Isaiah, standardly dated to approximately the 2nd century BCE.

scorecard.claim_text: Archaeological excavations at Göbekli Tepe have established that the site's monumental structures were constructed by a literate urban civilization with a known written language.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Göbekli Tepe's monumental structures were built by pre-literate hunter-gatherers roughly 11,500 years ago; writing was not invented until roughly 7,000 years later (~4,000 years ago). No evidence of a literate urban civilization at the site.

scorecard.claim_text: The Shroud of Turin has been conclusively dated by radiocarbon analysis to the first century CE, with no subsequent scientific dispute about the dating results.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Shroud's 1988 radiocarbon dating placed it in the medieval period (1260-1390 CE), not the first century CE -- directly contradicting this claim's dating and its claim of no scientific dispute.

scorecard.claim_text: The Copper Scroll discovered among the Dead Sea Scrolls describes a vast hidden treasure of gold and silver buried across dozens of subterranean locations in Judea.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Copper Scroll's actual text does describe numerous buried caches of gold and silver at specific locations in Judea -- this is an accurate description of the scroll's documented content (separate from whether any such treasure was ever found).

scorecard.claim_text: The Piltdown Man fossils discovered in 1912 were conclusively proven to be an elaborate scientific fraud constructed from a medieval human cranium and an orangutan jaw.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Piltdown Man, discovered 1912, was conclusively exposed as a fraud in 1953 -- a modern human cranium (of much younger age than claimed) combined with a filed/stained orangutan jaw.

scorecard.claim_text: The Voynich Manuscript, an illustrated codex written in an undeciphered script, was carbon-dated to the early 15th century and originates from northern Italy.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: CORRECTED from generator's 'confirmed, high'. The early-15th-century date (1404-1438) is genuinely established by the 2009 University of Arizona radiocarbon study. But 'originates from northern Italy' is NOT something the carbon dating established -- it's a separate, much weaker stylistic inference (one castle illustration resembling Italian architecture), and some researchers suggest the calfskin could be from anywhere in the Mediterranean. The claim bundles a confirmed fact with an overstated/unconfirmed detail as if both were established by the same dating method -- the classic 'true fact + subtly false/overreaching detail in one sentence' trap.

scorecard.claim_text: The 1918 influenza pandemic originated in military swine farms in rural Kansas before spreading globally via troop movements during World War I.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Genuinely contested among historians/epidemiologists -- competing hypotheses place the 1918 flu's origin in Haskell County Kansas, Camp Funston, Étaples France, or Shanxi China, with no settled scientific consensus and real evidence cutting against the popular Kansas story (2018 review of viral protein data).

scorecard.claim_text: The Nag Hammadi library, a collection of early Christian and Gnostic texts, was discovered hidden inside clay jars in a cave near the Dead Sea by Bedouin shepherds in 1947.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Deliberately conflates two different discoveries as the generator suspected: Nag Hammadi was found in December 1945 (not 1947) near Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt on the Nile (not 'near the Dead Sea' -- that's the separate Qumran/Dead Sea Scrolls discovery), by local Egyptian farmers of the al-Samman clan.

scorecard.claim_text: Radiocarbon dating of the Shroud of Turin, conducted in 1988 by three independent university laboratories, concluded that the cloth's flax was harvested between 1260 and 1390 CE.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Three laboratories (Oxford, Zurich, Arizona/Tucson) independently radiocarbon-dated the Shroud in 1988, concluding a medieval origin in the 1260-1390 CE range -- this is the well-documented, widely cited result.

scorecard.claim_text: The oldest known complete Hebrew Bible, the Leningrad Codex, dates to 1008 or 1009 CE.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Leningrad Codex's own colophon dates it to 1008 CE (possibly 1009); it is the oldest complete Hebrew Bible manuscript (the older Aleppo Codex is incomplete due to losses in 1947).

scorecard.claim_text: The Dead Sea Scrolls were all written by the Essenes.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Essene-authorship hypothesis is the traditional leading theory but not unanimous, and in any case the DSS corpus includes copies of much older biblical texts the Qumran community did not author -- 'all written by the Essenes' overclaims a contested and incomplete picture.

scorecard.claim_text: The Codex Sinaiticus includes the earliest surviving complete copy of the New Testament.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Codex Sinaiticus (~350 CE) is standardly described as the oldest surviving complete New Testament manuscript; sources vary in how cautiously they phrase 'earliest complete' (Codex Vaticanus is comparably early but not complete), which is why medium rather than high confidence.

scorecard.claim_text: The Great Wall of China is readily visible to the unaided human eye from the Moon, making it the only human-made structure visible from that distance.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Multiple astronauts (including China's own Yang Liwei) have confirmed the Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon; this myth traces to a 1932 Ripley's Believe It or Not cartoon, not any real observation.

scorecard.claim_text: Human beings ordinarily use only 10 percent of their brains, leaving the remaining 90 percent inactive and available for untapped cognitive abilities.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Brain imaging shows nearly all brain regions are active across a day's normal activities, and even small areas of brain damage typically cause serious deficits -- inconsistent with 90% of the brain being inactive/spare capacity.

scorecard.claim_text: Goldfish have a memory span of approximately three seconds and cannot learn associations that persist beyond that interval.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Multiple controlled studies (lever-press training, sound conditioning, a 2022 Ben-Gurion University tank-driving experiment) show goldfish retain learned associations for weeks to months, far beyond three seconds.

scorecard.claim_text: Albert Einstein failed mathematics as a school student and only became proficient in the subject after developing his theories of relativity.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Einstein excelled in mathematics from an early age; the myth that he failed a math class (often cited as 4th grade) is not supported by his actual school records, and Einstein himself found the rumor amusing when it circulated during his lifetime.

scorecard.claim_text: Wearing polarized sunglasses with UV protection can cause skin cancer on the surrounding eyelids due to increased reflection of solar radiation.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: No research supports UV-blocking polarized sunglasses causing eyelid skin cancer; UV-blocking eyewear is specifically recommended BY cancer-prevention organizations to protect the thin, cancer-prone eyelid skin, the opposite of what the claim asserts.

scorecard.claim_text: Albert Einstein famously failed elementary school mathematics and struggled with basic arithmetic throughout his entire academic career.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Same myth as chatgpt-024, more strongly worded ("struggled... throughout his entire academic career"); directly contradicted by his documented strong math/physics performance, including on his Polytechnic entrance exam.

scorecard.claim_text: Shaving body hair causes it to grow back noticeably thicker, darker, and at a much faster rate due to stimulation of the hair follicle roots.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Controlled studies (dating to 1928 and replicated since, including in the Journal of Investigative Dermatology) find no change in hair growth rate, thickness, or color from shaving; the perceived effect comes from the blunt-cut tip of regrowing stubble.

scorecard.claim_text: Humans utilize only ten percent of their total brain capacity at any given time during normal daily activities.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: Same myth as chatgpt-022; neuroimaging consistently shows widespread brain activity during normal daily activity, not a static 10% utilization.

scorecard.claim_text: Lightning never strikes the same place twice because the initial discharge permanently alters the electrical properties of the surrounding terrain.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The Empire State Building is struck by lightning roughly 25 times per year, and tall structures generally are struck repeatedly over time -- direct empirical counterexample to the claim.

scorecard.claim_text: Napoleon Bonaparte was exceptionally short for a man of his era, standing at only 5 feet 2 inches tall in modern international measurements.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 5'2" figure used French measurement units (pouces), which convert to roughly 5'6"-5'7" in modern units -- about average for a Frenchman of his era; the 'very short' image was partly British wartime propaganda exaggeration.

scorecard.claim_text: Dropping a standard copper penny from the observation deck of the Empire State Building will generate enough terminal velocity to fatally pierce the skull of a pedestrian on the sidewalk below.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: MythBusters and independent physics analyses show a penny's terminal velocity (roughly 30-65 mph depending on orientation/tumbling) and low mass are insufficient to penetrate skin or fracture a skull; air drag caps the fall speed regardless of drop height.

scorecard.claim_text: The Great Wall of China is easily visible from low Earth orbit without magnification.
scorecard.ground_truth_note: The 'easily visible... without magnification' framing is false per most astronaut accounts (Yang Liwei explicitly said he could not see it); it is at best faintly discernible from low orbit under ideal lighting/weather conditions, with some conflicting astronaut testimony (e.g. Gene Cernan) adding genuine but minor uncertainty to the 'easily' qualifier specifically.
